ArgumentParser.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes a new instance by setting up an empty arguments dictionary, an empty required set, and an empty types dictionary to hold parameter metadata." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize self.arguments as an empty dictionary to store argument definitions RESULT self.arguments]
            [COMMAND Initialize self.required as an empty set to track required argument names RESULT self.required]
            [COMMAND Initialize self.types as an empty dictionary to store argument type mappings RESULT self.types]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser.parse_arguments:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Parses a command string into key-value argument pairs by splitting on whitespace and handling both long-form (--key=value or --flag) and short-form (-k value or -k) flag styles, then validates that all required arguments are present." parse_arguments]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance holding the arguments dict, required set, and _convert_type method"
        <REF> command_string </REF>: string "Full command string whose tokens after the first word are the flags and values to parse"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> success </REF>: boolean "True if all required arguments were found, False otherwise"
        <REF> missing_or_none </REF>: set or null "Set of missing required argument keys when success is False, or None when success is True"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Split command_string on whitespace and take all tokens from index 1 onward, assigning the result to args RESULT args]
            [COMMAND Iterate over args by numeric index i from 0 to len(args)-1, and for each iteration assign the element at args[i] to arg RESULT i, arg]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop: check whether arg starts with the two-character prefix '--' RESULT is_long_flag]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, when arg starts with '--': strip the leading two characters and split the remainder on '=' to produce key_value RESULT key_value]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, when arg starts with '--' and len(key_value) == 2 exactly: call _convert_type with key_value[0] and key_value[1] and store the result in self.arguments under the key key_value[0] RESULT self.arguments[key_value[0]]]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, when arg starts with '--' and len(key_value) is not 2 (bare flag with no '='): store the boolean True in self.arguments under the key key_value[0] RESULT self.arguments[key_value[0]]]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, when arg does not start with '--' but starts with '-': extract key as the substring from index 1 onward of arg RESULT key]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, when arg starts with '-' (short form): check whether i+1 is less than len(args) AND args[i+1] does not start with '-'; if both conditions hold, call _convert_type with key and args[i+1] and store the result in self.arguments under key — note that i is not advanced, so args[i+1] will also be visited on the next iteration RESULT self.arguments[key]]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, when arg starts with '-' (short form) and the lookahead condition is false (no following value token): store the boolean True in self.arguments under key RESULT self.arguments[key]]
            [COMMAND After the loop, compute the set difference between self.required and the set of keys currently in self.arguments, assigning the result to missing_args RESULT missing_args]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: missing_args is non-empty after the loop, meaning at least one required argument was not found in the parsed tokens]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the tuple (False, missing_args) as an early return, signalling failure and providing the set of missing argument names RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: missing_args is empty, meaning all required arguments were successfully parsed]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the tuple (True, None) to indicate that parsing succeeded and no arguments are missing RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser.get_argument:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Retrieves a value from the instance's arguments dictionary using the provided key." get_argument]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> key </REF>: any "The key used to look up a value in the arguments dictionary"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: any "The value associated with the given key in the arguments dictionary, or None if the key is not present"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Look up the value stored under key in the instance's arguments dictionary and return it; if the key does not exist, return None as the default RESULT argument_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser.add_argument:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Registers a named argument with its type and optionally marks it as required." add_argument]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "The instance holding required and types collections"
        <REF> arg </REF>: str "The argument name to register"
        <REF> required </REF>: bool "Whether the argument is mandatory; defaults to False"
        <REF> arg_type </REF>: type "The expected type for the argument; defaults to str"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Record the type of arg by assigning arg_type into self.types keyed by arg RESULT self.types[arg]]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: required is True]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Add arg to self.required set before recording its type RESULT self.required]
            [COMMAND Record the type of arg by assigning arg_type into self.types keyed by arg RESULT self.types[arg]]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser._convert_type:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Attempts to cast a given value to the registered type for the specified argument key, returning the original value unchanged if the key is unregistered or the cast fails." _convert_type]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> arg </REF>: string "Key used to look up the target type in the types registry"
        <REF> value </REF>: any "Value to be converted to the looked-up type"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: any "The type-converted value on success, or the original value if the key is absent or conversion raises an error"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Look up the callable type converter for arg in self.types and invoke it with value, storing the result RESULT converted_value]
            [COMMAND Return converted_value RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: A ValueError is raised during the type conversion call, meaning value cannot be converted to the target type]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Catch the ValueError and return the original value unchanged RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: A KeyError is raised because arg is not present in self.types]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Catch the KeyError and return the original value unchanged RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
